figureNotes: The $1,500-or-15-percent rule, exclusion of active participants, and age-70½ restriction remain the ERISA rules. The 1976 Act added the $1,750 joint spousal deduction for taxable years beginning after December 31, 1976.

The IRS Bulletin records that 1981-and-earlier IRA deductions were limited to $1,500 or 15 percent of earned income, while one-earner married couples had a combined IRA limit; it contrasts the 1982 universal-eligibility change for participants covered by an employer plan. The unchanged SEP, §457, and §401(k) fields are the statutory rules enacted by Pub. L. 95-600.
The 25 percent of compensation limit is fixed by IRC 415(c)(1)(B) as then in effect; neither the IRS Cash or Deferred Arrangements table nor Publication 590 for these years prints it.
The 15 percent of compensation SEP limit is fixed by IRC 404(h)(1)(C) and 402(h)(2) as then in effect; the IRS Cash or Deferred Arrangements table does not print it.
Section 408A applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 1997; the 1997 data therefore has no Roth IRA and no pre-1997 fixed nonworking-spouse or one-earner cap.
IRS SEP/SARSEP Audit Techniques states that SBJPA prohibited new SARSEPs after December 31, 1996 while pre-1997 SARSEPs could continue.
ir-01-115 states the $130,000 "as added by Section 613 of EGTRRA"; pl-107-16 section 613(a)(1)(B) inserts it in IRC 416(i)(1)(A)(i), and section 613 applies to years beginning after December 31, 2001

pl-107-16 section 618(a) enacts the IRC 25B(b) table for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2001 (section 618(d)); the amounts were not indexed until Pub. L. 109-280 section 833(a), for taxable years beginning in a calendar year after 2006, so no notice states them
IRC 25B(d)(1)(A)-(C) as enacted by pl-107-16 section 618(a); pl-119-21 section 70116(a)(1) moves them to IRC 25B(d)(1)(B) and counts them only for taxable years beginning before January 1, 2027

Starts from Notice 2008-102, which cites them as §408A(c)(3)(C)(ii)(I) and (II); the same limits are §408A(c)(3)(B)(ii)(I) and (II) in the current Code, a relettering with no change in substance. Each end is the start plus the width fixed by §408A(c)(3)(A)(ii): $15,000, or $10,000 on a joint return or for a married individual filing a separate return, whose applicable dollar amount is zero under §408A(c)(3)(B)(ii)(III). See usc-26-408A.

Notice 2008-102 publishes the applicable dollar amounts under §219(g)(3)(B)(i) (joint return or qualifying widow(er)) and §219(g)(3)(B)(ii) (all other taxpayers other than married filing separately), which are the band starts; unlike the notices from 2013 on it does not print the ranges themselves. Each end is the start plus the width fixed by §219(g)(2)(A)(ii): $10,000, or $20,000 on a joint return. The married-filing-separately start is the zero applicable dollar amount at §219(g)(3)(B)(iii). See usc-26-219.

Start from Notice 2008-102 (§219(g)(7)(A)); the end is the start plus the $10,000 width that §219(g)(7)(B) substitutes for §219(g)(2)(A)(ii) in the spouse-covered case. See usc-26-219. The married-filing-separately band is published by no notice. §219(g)(7)(A) replaces only the joint applicable dollar amount, so a married individual filing a separate return keeps the zero fixed by §219(g)(3)(B)(iii), and §219(g)(7)(B) substitutes a $10,000 width for §219(g)(2)(A)(ii). §219(g)(4) removes spouses who lived apart for the whole year from the subsection altogether, which is why the data names this band 'living together'. See usc-26-219.

usc-26-402A. IRC 402A(e) was added by Pub. L. 117-328, div. T, title I, section 127(e)(1), and section 127(g) applies the amendments to "plan years beginning after December 31, 2023", making 2024 the first year a pension-linked emergency savings account may exist.

usc-26-402A. Notice 2023-75 does not state this figure. IRC 402A(e)(3)(A) fixes the limitation at "$2,500" and its flush text directs the Secretary to adjust it only "[i]n the case of contributions made in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024", so 2024 — the first effective year — carries the unadjusted statutory amount rather than an adjusted or carried-forward one.
